title: A systematic survey of distal element-gene regulatory interactions with Direct-Capture Targeted Perturb-seq
abstract: Identifying the impact of distal regulatory elements on gene expression is a core challenge in human genetics. Large-scale CRISPR screens have not captured lower effect size element-gene interactions due to selection bias and limited statistical power. We developed a framework for highly powered CRISPR screens, consisting of Direct-Capture Targeted Perturb-seq (DC-TAP-seq), unbiased target selection, and a pipeline accounting for statistical power. Surveying 9,666 random distal element-gene pairs revealed that most elements that reduced gene expression had effect sizes <10%, which prior studies were underpowered to detect. Out of the 84 interactions with negative effects, 45 (53.6%) occurred within 100 Kb of the promoter of the target gene. Many elements were bound by CTCF without classical enhancer chromatin, and both housekeeping and non-housekeeping genes had similar frequencies of distal regulatory elements. We highlight limitations of predictive models and suggest that new models consider elements with smaller effect sizes. Our study provides an expanded view of distal regulatory elements and a framework for building more comprehensive maps of distal regulation.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出 DC-TAP-seq 直接捕获式靶向 Perturb-seq 框架，结合无偏靶点选择与考虑统计功效的分析流程，首次系统性地检测远端元件-基因之间小效应（<10%）的调控关系。
llm.summary_zh: 该研究用 DC-TAP-seq 对 9,666 个随机远端元件-基因对进行高功效 CRISPR 扰动筛选，发现多数能降低基因表达的元件效应量小于 10%，既往研究因功效不足而漏检。结果显示负向调控相互作用中超过半数位于靶基因启动子 100 Kb 以内，且许多元件仅结合 CTCF 而无经典增强子染色质特征；作者同时指出现有预测模型的局限，建议新模型纳入小效应元件。
